Subject: Initial redline: MSA + Order Form — output attribution & training evidence

Hi Sofia and team,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attaching our redline to the MSA and the draft Order Form (BrightProduct_MSA_redline_v1.docx). Our core asks are:

- Explicit statement that BrightProduct will own downstream "productized" outputs for our internal product modules (we've marked the specific language).
- A carveout for internal telemetry and anonymized training data for model improvement under an agreed feedback license — but limited so it cannot be used to train public models.
- Evidence we can use in procurement: SOC2 artifact references, telemetry retention window, and a short list of technical controls around KV cache/derivative generation.

Two asks: can you confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with a non-derivative clause that prevents re-training of a public model with BrightProduct prompts/data, and provide a short template (one page) describing the evidence you can share for training safeguards? Our procurement regulator will need that.

Appreciate a quick turn — we have an internal procurement review on Wednesday.

Best,
Emma White
Senior Counsel, Legal — BrightProduct

- For telemetry and safeguards we can provide: SOC2 report references, a one-page operational summary of logging/retention, and a short checklist of runtime protections (prefix/KV caching policies, access controls).

Emma — following up with draft counterlanguage (attached: RW_response_marked.docx). Key points in the attached:

- Feedback license: we propose a limited, non-exclusive feedback license that allows Redwood to use aggregated telemetry to improve the platform, but excludes using BrightProduct confidential customer content to train or fine-tune models that are made generally available.
- Output attribution: suggested wording clarifies that BrightProduct owns derivative outputs only when explicitly identified in the Order Form and where use of the output is productization of BrightProduct IP (we propose a checkbox in the Order Form).
- Evidence and audit: we'll provide SOC2 references and an operations summary; we cannot share production logs but can provide an access-control and retention statement and an ops contact for an evidence handoff.

Questions for procurement: is a signed NDA addendum acceptable for more detailed evidence review, or do you prefer a vendor assessment (third-party SaaS security questionnaire)?

Laura Bennett

Emma/Team — adding an operational checklist and clarifications on how we enforce the proposed limits. Short summary below; full checklist will be in the 1-pager.

Operational summary (high level):
- Model training: we do not include customer-provided prompts/content in public model training unless there is an explicit opt-in in the Order Form. For dedicated/private deployments we can further isolate training pipelines.
- KV/prefix caching: we persist KV caches only per-customer session in Dedicated/Private; hosted API has configurable TTLs and opt-out flags.
- Anonymization & telemetry: we aggregate telemetry and redact PII before use in platform-level analytics.
- Evidence handoff: we can provide a one-page operations summary + SOC2 pointer. For deeper technical due diligence we prefer an NDA + redacted sample artifacts or a security questionnaire.

Attachment: operational_evidence_template.txt (draft) — I'll drop the draft into our shared drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Redwood-Evidence-Templates

I'll be on the call Monday to walk through the checklist.

—Sean
